prompts.local:
Use case: historical-scene.
Asset type: production game texture, the FIRST and authoritative highest-detail tile in a new impact-first Earth surface set for a Chicxulub asteroid simulation.
Create a NEW exquisitely sharp photorealistic satellite-style ALBEDO TEXTURE of the Yucatan impact region BEFORE impact, an illustrative late-Cretaceous reconstruction. This local tile is the source from which later regional and global maps will be outpainted, so give it distinctive coherent organic geography.
Projection/framing: square 2048x2048 preferred, perfectly vertical overhead, north up, flat equirectangular crop, no perspective, no visible globe. Geographic bounds longitude -95.5 to -83.5 degrees, latitude 15.4 to 27.4 north. Exact image center represents 21.4 north, 89.5 west and MUST be unbroken shallow turquoise sea over limestone shelf, not land and not an island. The center is a future impact location, not marked.
Geography: broad subdued turquoise carbonate shelf and finely branching underwater pale sediment channels across the center and northern half, transitioning into dark navy open ocean toward the upper edge. Irregular low limestone shoreline mostly south of center, richly detailed dark green forest and wetlands on the southern landmass, deeper blue water toward eastern side. A plausible shallow marine setting, not a precise scientific palaeomap. Avoid dozens of invented tiny islands.
Materials: extraordinarily fine natural limestone grain, nonrepeating branching sandbars underwater, thin sediment ripples and shoals visible THROUGH clear water, tiny forest canopy clusters, small drainage channels and complex wetland margins ON LAND. Distinct sharp coastline with fine natural detail; restrained real satellite colors, medium dark forest greens, muted warm limestone and sand, teal shallows and navy deep water. No blurry smooth airbrush, no large lumpy relief, no artificial grain.
Lighting: neutral diffuse albedo, no highlights, no directional shadows, no sun glint, no atmospheric haze.
Constraints: full bleed complete square texture; flat map only; no crater, concentric rings, explosion, impact scars, volcano, target marker, labels, text, scale bar, grid, frame, clouds, city, buildings, roads, boats, border, watermark. Highest native detail and crispness.
prompts.region:
Use case: compositing.
Asset type: middle level of a three-level Earth ALBEDO texture for a 3D globe.
Input image 1: AUTHORITATIVE edit target/insert, the newly created local impact-region texture; it is not a loose style reference.
Primary request: OUTPAINT OUTWARD from this exact image to show FOUR TIMES its width and FOUR TIMES its height in geographic coverage. The ENTIRE original image, reduced to exactly 25% of the new canvas width and height, occupies the exact central square x=37.5%..62.5%, y=37.5%..62.5%. Preserve the original geography in that square, including all its distinctive pale branching submerged sediment channels, forest coastline, turquoise shallow sea and navy sea. Do not reinterpret it, rotate it, move it or enlarge that inset. No inset border; connect its edges seamlessly to newly generated terrain.
New canvas: square, highest native resolution, preferred 2048x2048, flat equirectangular map, north up, zero perspective, never a spherical globe. Geographic extent -113.5 to -65.5 longitude, -2.6 to 45.4 latitude. Center stays 21.4N 89.5W, shallow sea at the future impact site.
Outpaint surrounding illustrative late-Cretaceous geography: southern North America and a broad Gulf to north of the inset, Mexico to west, Caribbean marine region to east, northern South America at lower right, eastern Pacific in lower left. Broad forests and natural limestone coasts, marine shelves, dark navy deep ocean. Match source albedo colors exactly and retain appropriate scale: local fine sediment becomes much smaller, broad continental forms now visible.
Lighting/style: sharp photorealistic satellite albedo with neutral diffuse light, restrained greens, limestone tones, turquoise shelves, navy blue ocean. No baked glare, shadows, bump-lit mountainous lumps, clouds, atmosphere. Illustrative artistic reconstruction, no claim of exact palaeogeography.
Constraints: No crater, explosion, island at exact center, circle, target, rings, text, borders, labels, grid, roads/cities, duplicated local patch or hard rectangular seams. The local source is the seed; grow a coherent larger world around it. Full-bleed square texture.
prompts.world:
Use case: compositing.
Asset type: final GLOBAL EARTH EQUIRECTANGULAR ALBEDO TEXTURE, third step of an impact-first terrain texture set.
Input image 1: authoritative REGIONAL SEED IMAGE to preserve in its proper location while outpainting the entire rest of Earth. The previous work started at the Yucatan shallow-sea impact site and expanded outward; now expand from this region to a COMPLETE world.
Canvas: exactly 2:1 wide landscape, preferred 4096x2048 or highest native resolution. It is a FLAT rectangular equirectangular UV texture map, NOT a globe render. Horizontal covers longitude -180 at left to +180 at right, vertical +90 latitude top to -90 bottom; Greenwich at horizontal center; equator vertical center. North up. Fill every pixel, zero margins.
Registration: source region depicts longitudes -113.5 to -65.5 and latitudes +45.4 to -2.6. Place it approximately within x=18.4722%..31.8056%, y=24.7778%..51.4444% of the final canvas (a square in physical pixels). Its center/future impact coordinate is x=25.1389%, y=38.1111%. Preserve the recognizable turquoise sediment shelf, dark green Yucatan shoreline and branching pale underwater channels at that spot. Do not move the Americas to the center of the map. Do not enlarge the Gulf/Yucatan region disproportionately.
Outpaint: a coherent complete artistic late-Cretaceous Earth with all continental landmasses and continuous oceans, broadly recognizable continental arrangement, shallow inland North American seaway, fragmented warm European shelves, Africa, South America, Asia, India in the Indian Ocean, Australia and forested southern polar continent. Geographic detail is illustrative rather than a scientific reconstruction. Match the seed's muted forest greens, warm limestone earth, turquoise shallow shelf, deep navy ocean. Ocean floor detail only subtle; uniform unlit oceans. The whole planet should read as naturally connected large land masses, not a collage.
Projection: polar features stretched horizontally as required by equirectangular mapping; top and bottom edge each consistent in color across its width, no chopped land fragments. Left and right image edges must join seamlessly across the Pacific with matching ocean color and pattern. No black corners.
Lighting: even diffuse unlit albedo, no cloud veil, no cast shadows, no baked sunlight or specular reflection, no atmospheric rim. Fine sharp varied land detail with natural coastal gradients.
Constraints: preserve the regional seed's visual identity and geography, connect surrounding terrain without visible rectangles or pasted borders. No crater, impact scars, target marker, circles, explosion, text, labels, borders, latitude-longitude lines, map symbols, roads/cities, watermark, clouds, photograph frame. OUTPUT ONE FULL RECTANGULAR WORLD MAP, NOT A SPHERICAL EARTH.
